summary: Ramesh Chandra Majumdar was an Indian historian and Indologist who studied at Ravenshaw, Brojomohun, Ripon, Surendranath, and Presidency colleges, completing his dissertation at the University of Calcutta. He held professorships and administrative roles at Dhaka, BHU, Nagpur, Chicago, and Pennsylvania.

Ramesh Shankar Gupte was an Indian historian and Indologist. In 1967, he headed the Department of History and Ancient Indian Culture at Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University and was a visiting lecturer at Wake Forest, Salem, and Winston-Salem State.

Ramin Etesami is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College around 2015, where he was supervised by Geshe Lozang Jamspal and Krishna Ghosh Della Santina.
Ramon N. Prats is a Tibetologist. He was affiliated with Himalayan and Inner Asian Resources in 1999 and Pompeu Fabra University in 2017.
Randall Studstill is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied under Steven D. Goodman and completed his doctoral work under the supervision of Richard K. Payne.

Randy J. LaPolla is a linguist and sinologist who studied at the University of California, Berkeley under James Alan Matisoff. He served as a professor at City University of Hong Kong and held a post at Beijing Normal University, Zhuhai.

Rangama Chandawimala is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied traditionally under Attaragama Gnanawimala. He earned a PhD from The University of Hong Kong under the supervision of Jing Yin and co-supervisor Kakkapalliye Anuruddha Thera.

Rangjung Rigpe Dorje (1924–1981) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology master. He studied under the 13th Dalai Lama, Situ Pema Wangchok Gyalpo, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Karsé Kongtrul, Tubten Chokyi Dorje, and Karma Shedrub Chokyi Sengge.

Raniero Gnoli (1930–2025) was an Italian Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Giuseppe Tucci and Mario Praz. He served as Professor of Indology at Sapienza University of Rome from 1964 to 2000.
Raoul Birnbaum is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who served as a professor of Buddhist studies at the University of California, Santa Cruz, with publications attested in 2003 and 2017.
Raphael Kühner (1802–1878) was a German linguist who was educated at Ernestinum Gotha and studied at the University of Göttingen from circa 1821 to 1824.

Raphael von Koeber (1848–1923) was a philosopher who studied at the Moscow Conservatory, Heidelberg University, and the University of Jena. He held a post at the University of Tokyo beginning in 1893.

Rasiklal Chhotalal Parikh (1897–1982) was an Indologist and historian. Educated at Fergusson College under R. D. Ranade, and taught by Sukhlal Sanghvi and Muni Jinvijaya, he was a Sanskrit and history professor at Gujarat Vidyapith.

Rasmus Rask (1787–1832) was a Danish linguist, Indologist, and Central Asian scholar educated at Odense Katedralskole and the University of Copenhagen, where he later held posts as librarian and professor of literary history and Eastern languages.
Ratna Vajra Rinpoche is a Tibetan Buddhist master in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga, whom he succeeded in 2017.

Ravi M. Gupta is an Indologist and religious studies scholar educated at Boise State University and the University of Oxford. He taught at Florida, Centre College, and William & Mary before becoming Charles Redd Chair at Utah State University.

Ravindra Singh Bisht is an Indian archaeologist who studied at the University of Lucknow, the Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Institute of Archaeology, and Kumaun University. He served in the Archaeological Survey of India, eventually rising to Director General.

Sir Raymond West (1832–1912) was an Indologist who studied under Martin Haug. He served as a judge of the Bombay High Court, Vice Chancellor of the University of Mumbai, and Reader in Indian Law at the University of Cambridge.
Reb Anderson is a Buddhist studies teacher who studied under Shunryu Suzuki and Richard Baker. He succeeded Baker and served as abbot of the San Francisco Zen Center from circa 1986 to 1995.
Reb Gongwa Jamyang Chökyi Lodrö studied under traditional teachers Khenpo Jigme Phuntsok and Khenpo Tsultrim Lodro.
